title: Measuring length in centimetres and metres
examples: How do I measure with a ruler?
How many centimetres are in a metre?

items.label: Door
items.ask: How many centimetres are in a metre?

explain.say: How long is your pencil? Longer than a key, shorter than a shoe? Look at the bars: each one shows a real length in centimetres. A centimetre is about as wide as your little fingernail.

draw.text: Measuring length in centimetres and metres

items.label: Door
items.ask: How many centimetres are in a metre?

explain.say: See the ruler bar? A school ruler is usually 30 centimetres long. To measure, put the 0 mark at one end of the thing, and read the number at the other end. Can you find the 0 on your ruler?

items.label: Door
items.ask: How many centimetres are in a metre?

explain.say: This pencil is 17 centimetres. We write it 17 cm for short. That is a bit more than half a ruler. Which bar is the shortest?

items.label: Door
items.ask: How many centimetres are in a metre?

explain.say: For long things we use metres. 100 centimetres make 1 metre. This door is 200 centimetres, which is 2 metres. A child might be 130 centimetres tall. Is that more or less than one metre?

items.label: Door
items.ask: How many centimetres are in a metre?

explain.say: Great measuring! Wow: the metre was first set in France in the 1790s, as a tiny part of the distance from the North Pole to the equator. Challenge: guess how long your bed is in metres, then measure it!

items.label: Door
items.ask: How many centimetres are in a metre?

faq.q: How do I measure with a ruler?
faq.a: Line up the 0 mark with one end of the object, keep the ruler straight, and read the number at the other end. That number is the length in centimetres.
asks: How do I use a ruler?

faq.a: A standard school ruler is 30 centimetres long. Some short rulers are 15 centimetres.
asks: How many centimetres is a ruler?

faq.q: How many centimetres are in a metre?
faq.a: There are 100 centimetres in 1 metre. A metre is about as tall as a 4-year-old child.

faq.q: Why do we start at 0 and not 1?
faq.a: The 0 mark is the very start of the length. If you start at 1, you miss the first centimetre, and your answer is 1 too big.

faq.q: When should I use metres instead of centimetres?
faq.a: Use centimetres for small things like a pencil or a book. Use metres for big things like a room, a door or a swimming pool.

facts: The metre was first defined in France in the 1790s as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator.

quiz.say: How many centimetres are in 3 metres?
quiz.show: How many centimetres are in 3 metres?
quiz.why: Each metre is 100 centimetres, so 3 metres is 300 centimetres.

wrong.0: 30 would be right only if a metre were 10 centimetres.
wrong.2: 3 is the number of metres, not centimetres.

quiz.say: A pencil starts at 0 and ends at 14 on a ruler. How long is it?
quiz.show: A pencil starts at 0 and ends at 14 on a ruler. How long is it?
quiz.why: Starting at 0, the end mark gives the length: 14 centimetres.

wrong.1: 14 metres would be longer than a bus!
